subtype: Approach: checking against a source of truth [Thinking]
passage: Supervisor's note. I sat in on Vaibhav's prep for the client summary on Wednesday. The AI summary of the industry report read smoothly and carried three figures and two citations. Vaibhav said aloud, 'These tools sometimes invent things that sound right, so I'll check each one against the original.' Vaibhav opened the report and went through them one by one. Two figures matched. One number was off, 14 where the report said 41, and a citation pointed to a paper Vaibhav could not find at all. Both were removed. Tanvir from sales, waiting on the document, asked why it was late, and Vaibhav said, 'One line in the summary wasn't real.' I asked Vaibhav to note the check in the file so the next person does the same.

qa.q: How many figures and citations did the AI summary carry?
qa.a: It carried three figures and two citations.

qa.q: Why might Vaibhav feel uneasy trusting the smooth-reading AI summary, and what shows it?
qa.a: Vaibhav was wary that such tools sometimes invent things that sound right, so a smooth read was not proof.

qa.q: What could Vaibhav add to the checking, and why?
qa.a: Vaibhav could ask a colleague to spot-check two items, since a second pair of eyes may catch what a tired person misses.

qa.q: How might Tanvir have seen the delay?
qa.a: Tanvir was probably impatient waiting, but the reason shows the check kept a false line away from the client. 🙂

grounding: Shows an analyst checking each figure and citation from an AI summary against the original report before it goes into a client document.

passage:
Wednesday, 9.40 p.m.
Almost sent it. The AI summary of the sixty-page market report looked perfect: five bullet points, three figures, two citations. Rehana wanted the client note by 10 tomorrow.
But I've read enough about these tools making things up, so I went back to the original report, figure by figure. Market size: 4,200 crore. Matches page 12. Growth rate: the summary said 18%. The report says 18% for one segment only; overall it's 11%. Citation two: a 'government survey, 2022' that isn't in the report at all. I searched. I can't find it anywhere.
So two of five points would have gone to the client wrong. I fixed the growth rate, cut the fake citation and put page numbers next to every figure.
Tomorrow I'll tell Rehana what I found. Tired, but glad.
Kavitha

qa.q: What does the report say overall growth is?
How does Kavitha feel at the end of the evening?
qa.a: Kavitha feels tired but glad and relieved, having caught two wrong points before they reached the client.

qa.q: What else could Kavitha suggest to Rehana for future summaries?
qa.a: Kavitha could suggest that every AI summary carry page numbers for each figure, so anyone can check it against the source quickly.

qa.q: How might the client have been affected if the note had gone out unchecked?
qa.a: The client could have acted on a wrong growth rate and a citation that doesn't exist, damaging trust in the firm.

grounding: It shows an analyst verifying each figure and citation from an AI summary against the original report before it goes into a client note.

Nilesh: sending the board deck in 20 min. used the AI to summarise the audit report, saved me 3 hours 🙌
Raghav: did you check the numbers against the report?
Nilesh: it's a summary of the report. it's the report's numbers
Raghav: not always. these tools sometimes invent things that sound right
Nilesh: fine, checking
[15 min later]
Nilesh: ok. revenue figure correct. cost savings figure wrong, it says 14 crore, report says 1.4
Nilesh: and it quotes 'section 7.3'. the report only has 6 sections
Raghav: that's the kind of thing
Nilesh: the board would have seen a number ten times too big. with my name on it
Raghav: check every number and quote against the source before anything goes out. every time
Nilesh: yeah. pushing the deck by 30 min. going line by line

qa.q: What does the report say the cost savings were?
How did Nilesh feel on finding the error?
qa.a: Nilesh felt alarmed and a little embarrassed, realising the board would have seen a wrong number with Nilesh's name on it.

qa.q: What habit is Raghav suggesting, and why does it work?
qa.a: Checking every number and quote against the source every time, because AI summaries can sound right while inventing numbers or sections.

qa.q: How might the board be affected by Nilesh's check?
qa.a: They get a deck they can trust, thirty minutes later, instead of deciding on a number ten times too big.

grounding: It shows someone checking every figure and reference in an AI summary against the original report before it goes out.
